questions.prompt: What is the role of `using Base::log;` inside a derived class that defines `void log(int)` when `Base` defines `void log(double)`?
options: It marks Base::log as virtual so Derived can override it.
It prevents Derived::log(int) from hiding Base::log(double) during name lookup.
It enables Argument-Dependent Lookup across Base's namespace.
It suppresses access checking on private members of Base.
questions.explanation: Without `using Base::log;`, unqualified lookup finds `log` in `Derived` and stops before inspecting `Base`, hiding `Base::log(double)`. A using-declaration introduces the base overloads into `Derived` scope so overload resolution can choose among all of them.

questions.prompt: Which call disables Argument-Dependent Lookup when invoking a free function `process` on an object `v` of type `geom::Vec`?
options: process(v);
using geom::process; process(v);
(process)(v);
a + b; // where operator+ is a hidden friend
questions.explanation: ADL only applies when the postfix expression of a function call is an unqualified-id. Wrapping `process` in parentheses `(process)(v)` or qualifying it (`geom::process(v)`) suppresses ADL.

questions.prompt: What happens when calling `w.emit(42)` on this class?
options: It calls public emit(double) because private overloads are hidden from callers.
It is ambiguous because both overloads accept 42.
It compiles with a warning and converts 42 to double.
It fails to compile with an access error because overload resolution selects private emit(int) before checking access.
questions.explanation: Name lookup collects all `emit` members regardless of access specifier, overload resolution selects `emit(int)` as an exact match over `emit(double)`, and access control runs last and rejects the call to private `emit(int)`.

questions.prompt: Why does `return value;` inside `Derived<T>::get()` fail to compile when `Base<T>` defines `int value = 1;`?
options: Because `value` is a non-dependent name, Phase 1 lookup runs at template definition time and does not inspect dependent base class Base<T>.
Because data members of template bases are always private unless marked protected.
Because `const` member functions cannot access inherited non-const fields.
Because ADL only finds functions, not data members.
questions.explanation: Under two-phase name lookup ([temp.res]), non-dependent unqualified names inside a template are looked up during Phase 1 without inspecting dependent base classes like `Base<T>`, since an explicit specialization could redefine `Base<T>`. Writing `this->value` or `Base<T>::value` makes it dependent.

questions.prompt: Under [basic.lookup.argdep], which declaration found by ordinary unqualified lookup prevents ADL from running for `swap(a, b)`?
options: Only if `swap(int&, int&)` is a better match than `ns::swap`.
A block-scope function declaration that is not a using-declaration suppresses ADL completely, making `swap(a, b)` ill-formed.
A `using std::swap;` declaration inside `run` suppresses ADL just like a function declaration.
ADL still runs and finds `ns::swap` because `int&` cannot bind to `ns::Item`.
questions.explanation: [basic.lookup.argdep] specifies that if ordinary unqualified lookup finds a block-scope function declaration (that is NOT a using-declaration), a class member, or a non-function, ADL is not performed. By contrast, `using std::swap;` is a using-declaration and intentionally allows ADL.

questions.prompt: Why does `std::vector<geom::Vec>` allow ADL on `f(vec)` to search `namespace geom` in addition to `namespace std`?
options: Because `std::vector` places a `using namespace geom;` directive inside `std`.
Because ADL always searches every namespace declared before the call site.
Because associated namespaces of a class template specialization include the associated namespaces of its template type arguments.
Because `geom::Vec` inherits from `std::vector` implicitly.
questions.explanation: Under [basic.lookup.argdep], the set of associated namespaces and classes of a class template specialization includes not only its own enclosing namespace and bases, but also the associated namespaces and classes of its template type arguments (and template template arguments).
